newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky sees possible infotech pact at WTO meet.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky sees possible infotech pact at WTO meet.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday that she believes that a global agreement eliminating tariffs on information technology can be concluded at next week's meeting of World Trade Organization ministers in Singapore.

Barshefsky told reporters that the support of Asia-Pacific leaders for the global agreement to do away with tariffs on information technology by 2000 set the stage "for what should be doable" at the WTO meeting.
"The ITA should be able to be concluded at Singapore," Barshefsky said. But she said more work was needed by negotiators on product coverage and the staging of tariff reductions.
Barshefsky also expressed concern about the stance of the European Union in the information technology negotiations.
"More progress will have to be made attitudinally, particularly with regard to the EU," Barshefsky said.
She said she was concerned that the European Union has sent out recent signals that it may not be important to conclude the global technology agreement by the WTO meeting.
"We have still a very schizophrenic Europe and that won't do if this is going to conclude at Singapore," Barshefsky said.
On her way to Singapore, Barshefsky plans to stop in Tokyo to meet with Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka in an effort to resolve a dispute over insurance by a December 15 deadline.

Barshefsky said that settlement of the dispute hinges on deregulation of the primary life and casuality sectors, dominated by Japanese firms, before opening up the so-called third sector specialty insurance, where foreign firms play a big role.
"We are hopeful that they will be responsive to the necessity for initiatives with respect to significant primary sector deregulation," Barshefsky said.
"Without that there can be no settlement of the insurance dispute."
